dedupe_keys.name: enhanced national scale urban tree canopy cover dataset for the united states

description: This USGS data release improves the 30 m National Land Cover Database tree canopy cover product inside US urban areas, where the national product underestimates fine-grained urban trees, by training random forest models on high-resolution land cover. It covers all 2020 Census Urban Areas in the conterminous United States, about 273,844 square kilometres, as a 30 m raster of canopy percentage from 0 to 100 with a nominal 2011 date, trained on high-resolution land cover for 71 urban areas; the model estimated canopy within 3 per cent for 62 of them and added 13.4 per cent more city-level canopy on average. It was produced by L. M. Corro, K. J. Bagstad and co-authors as a US Geological Survey data release, published on 10 February 2025 and described in Scientific Data. It is available for download from ScienceBase as a cloud optimised GeoTIFF with a data dictionary, FGDC metadata, training data and Jupyter notebook code, under CC0 1.0 and free of charge. Caveats: the authors state it should not be used to locate individual trees, and the nominal date is 2011. It supports urban heat, stormwater and ecosystem service modelling and equity analysis of green infrastructure; a related record is the i-Tree model suite.
